original.text: lus ljon shing mchog yan lag rnam lnga la/ /g.yo ba'i sems la sgra gcan rab tu 'jug /brtan par mdzod cig bde chen yongs kyi tshad/ /lU yis smras pa bla ma la zhus mkhyen/ /ma lus ting 'dzin rnams kyis ci zhig bya/

paraphrase: Lūipa's song: the body is a fine tree with five branches; Rāhu enters the fickle mind; make it steady — the measure of great bliss; Lūi says, ask the guru and know: what use are all the samādhis? Pulling out bliss by the root one surely dies; abandon the scheming, deceitful mind that composes (and) binds with the noose to the side of emptiness; Lūi sees by his own meditation; bringing down moon and sun, set them above.
speaker: Lūipa
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan
notes: Read in the Tibetan of Munidatta's commentary; the Old Bengali opening ('kāa taruvara pañca vi ḍāla') is recalled, not read. Several lines of the Tibetan are obscure to the unit.

paraphrase: Kāṇha's song to the Ḍombī: 'O Ḍombī, your hut is outside the city' — the outcaste woman who lives beyond the town and whom the shaven brahmin youth touches in passing is taken, in the commentary, as the avadhūtī / Nairātmyā beyond conceptual society.
notes: Reference from memory; not located in a local text. The commentarial reading is Munidatta's per memory.

paraphrase: Kukkuripa's song ends: 'This song Kukkuripa sang — among ten million, could it enter the heart of even one?' (preceded by riddling images of the house with seven doors, the thief at midnight and the mother-in-law asleep).
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan
notes: Munidatta's commentary then cites Kāṇha: one in ten million may understand.

paraphrase: Śabara's song: high, high is the mountain where the Śabara girl lives, wearing peacock feathers and a garland of guñjā berries; the mad Śabara, the Śabarī — the mountain girl is the innate (Nairātmyā) with whom the yogin dwells.
notes: Reference from memory; not located in a local text.

paraphrase: Ḍheṇḍhaṇa's riddle song: my house is on the hill with no neighbours, there is no rice in the pot yet guests keep coming — paradoxes pointing beyond ordinary sense.
notes: Reference from memory; not located in a local text.

paraphrase: Cāṭila's song: the river of existence is deep and swift; build a bridge (of the teacher's instruction / of emptiness and compassion) and cross; those who go to the far shore do not return.
notes: Reference from memory; not located in a local text. Poet and number recalled (low).

paraphrase: Bhusuku's song of the hunted deer: the deer's own flesh is its enemy; hunted on all sides, it cannot escape; Bhusuku says the one who understands is not caught.
notes: Reference from memory; not located in a local text.

paraphrase: Munidatta's commentary ends: the vajra songs of the siddhas, with their commentary, were composed by the master Munidatta for those who would clearly know reality; translated by Grags pa rgyal mtshan at Yambu in Nepal, instructed by Kīrticandra.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan
